subject: Hardware tuning profiles pack — kickoff + owners + runtime-1.22 target
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Hardware tuning profiles pack — kickoff + owners + runtime-1.22 target

Team — kicking off the “hardware tuning profiles pack” work so we can stop treating runtime tuning as tribal knowledge per GPU pool and make it versioned + observable.

Goal (high level)
- Ship a vetted, versioned profile pack for H100 + L40S (and B200 preview) that selects the best-known kernel/scheduler/memory defaults per SKU and workload bucket.
- Document expected behavior + tradeoffs so Infra/SRE and customer-facing teams can roll safely.

Target
- Land in runtime-1.22 train (feature-flagged initially; default enablement is a separate go/no-go with SRE signoff).

Owners / proposed leads
- Program mgmt + tracking: Talia
- Runtime architecture / selection rules: Noah
- Kernel variants + telemetry: Hiro
- Scheduler buckets + queue policy: Sofia
- Observability dashboards + alert spec: Allison
- Rollout guardrails/runbook: Sean + Rafael
- Release train / versioning hygiene: Connor
- Infra fleet constraints + compatibility matrix: Neha + Irene

Project epic + scope
- Linear epic: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4921
  - Schema + validation: ENG-4922
  - Rollout plan: ENG-4933

Early Confluence outline
- I put a stub page up so we can converge on the doc set (expected behavior per SKU, schema, rollout/runbook, benchmarking):
  https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/2418937857/Hardware+tuning+profiles+pack+overview

Two decisions we need early (please reply with constraints):
1) Where selection logic lives: runtime-only vs control-plane assisted. (My bias is runtime selection for determinism + fewer config drift issues.)
2) Compatibility gates: what driver/CUDA spread we must support per SKU (and what we hard-fail vs warn), especially for early B200 nodes.

Next steps
- Talia will send a 30-min kickoff early next week. Please come with:
  - Known pain points (tail latency regressions, OOM/fragmentation patterns, kernel fallback weirdness)
  - Fleet constraints (driver/CUDA baseline, MIG policy, PCIe vs SXM differences)
  - What we must measure to make this safe (queueing vs compute split, kernel choice counters, fragmentation estimates)

Thanks — this is foundational to making performance predictable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 10:04 AM PT
Subject: Re: Hardware tuning profiles pack — kickoff + owners + runtime-1.22 target

+1. From Infra side, a few constraints to bake in from day 1:

- Fleet heterogeneity is real right now:
  - H100 is split across SXM and PCIe instance types (perf differences under prefill-heavy loads).
  - L40S pools have a wider driver spread than we’d like due to customer scheduling constraints.
- MIG: Hosted H100 is no-MIG; Dedicated varies (some customers asked for MIG, we’ve allowed case-by-case). We need the profile pack to (a) detect MIG and (b) refuse unsafe defaults / require explicit pin.
- B200: we will have early nodes with driver/CUDA variance during bring-up. We should hard-gate “default enablement” on B200, and require explicit profile_version pin + explicit allowlist of known-good combos.

Re: selection logic location — runtime-based selection is preferable to us, as long as the runtime can log “what it saw” (SKU, driver, cuda runtime) and the exact profile_id/version it picked. That will prevent a lot of back-and-forth during incidents.

Irene and I can provide a concrete list of instance types + current driver/CUDA baselines for H100/L40S before kickoff.

Neha


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 10:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Hardware tuning profiles pack — kickoff + owners + runtime-1.22 target

From SRE perspective, two “must haves” for runtime-1.22 if we want to canary this safely:

1) Kill switch semantics
- Ability to roll back to previous profile pack version quickly (and ideally per cohort / per region), without requiring a runtime binary rollback.
- Clear logs + /health (or equivalent) reporting the active profile_version/profile_id.

2) Rollout gates + required signals
- We should define upfront which SLO deltas block rollout (p95 and p99 latency, error rate, and timeouts).
- Required dashboard panels for canary:
  - scheduler_queue_ms (separate from compute)
  - kernel fallback counters / kernel choice distribution
  - OOMs + fragmentation signals (even if approximate)
  - GPU util + memory headroom estimates

If we align on those, Rafael and I can draft the canary cohort plan + escalation/rollback runbook.

Also: please keep Dedicated opt-in for profile changes by default. We can’t surprise customers with tail changes without a communication plan.

Sean


From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Noah Patel <noah.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 11:11 AM PT
Subject: Re: Hardware tuning profiles pack — kickoff + owners + runtime-1.22 target

Works for me.

One release process question we should settle in kickoff:
- Are we treating the profile pack artifact as versioned “data” shipped with runtime (e.g., embedded JSON/YAML + checksums), or as an independently updatable artifact?

If independently updatable, we need:
- A signing / provenance story (even internal), and
- Clear backport policy to LTS branches (profile fixes vs code fixes).

If shipped with runtime, it simplifies provenance but makes rollback slower unless we build a “previous pack” fallback into the binary.

Either way, I’d like us to adopt changelog discipline for profile changes (what changed + expected perf impact + how to revert).

Connor


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 12:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Hardware tuning profiles pack — kickoff + owners + runtime-1.22 target

Thanks all — this is exactly the input we need.

A few quick aligns before Talia schedules:

- Selection logic: we’ll do runtime-based selection (deterministic), but include explicit override/pin support for Dedicated/Private with guardrails + audit trail.
- Compatibility: agree on hard gates for “unknown” driver/CUDA combos (especially B200). Neha/Irene please bring the current spread + what we consider “supported” vs “warn-only.”
- Rollout: agree Dedicated stays opt-in initially. Hosted will be small canary cohort with a kill switch. Sean/Rafael, let’s define the exact rollback lever(s) as part of ENG-4933.

Connor — good call on artifact packaging. My current leaning:
- Ship the pack with runtime for 1.22 (simplify provenance and avoid control-plane coordination), BUT include:
  - Ability to pin an older pack version that is still bundled (N-1) and
  - A fast runtime config flag to revert to baseline defaults.
We can revisit “independent artifact updates” once we have the basic versioning/guardrails working.

Allison — please ensure the Confluence outline includes required dashboards + label/tag plan (profile_id, sku, driver).

Talia — please set kickoff for 30 mins; agenda:
1) Confirm scope + non-goals
2) Profile schema fields we consider v1
3) Compatibility gating rules
4) Benchmark matrix + acceptance thresholds
5) Rollout plan + SLO gates

— Mateo
